messages:
lucy_cs: Hi team — BrightBeam on Dedicated EU2 is seeing recurring p95 latency spikes and intermittent 429s for their model endpoint after warmup. Customer says errors start ~10m after cold-start and correlate with a burst of requests. Sample req id: rb-ff12a3. Headline from customer: "sudden tail latency > 2s for generation, then a handful of 429s".

lucy_cs: Quick paste of their summary: 
- Pool: eu2-dedicated-34
- Model: open-vicuna-30b-quant (variant q4)
- MIG partitions: fractional (1g.10gb + 2g.20gb on same host)
- Observed: p95 jumps from 80ms -> 2200ms, then some 429s.

dan_engineer: Thanks Lucy. Can you attach the backend pool id and the tenant slot id? Also, do we have node-level metrics (SM util, mem bw) around the spike window?

lucy_cs: Pool id: pool-34-eu2, slot: brightbeam-102. I pulled the timeline from console:
```
2026-03-16T09:12:10Z request spike (burst 600 req/min)
2026-03-16T09:12:35Z p95 climb begins
2026-03-16T09:22:18Z 10x 429 responses over 30s
2026-03-16T09:22:50Z autoscaler: added 1 slot (delay 45s)
2026-03-16T09:23:40Z p95 recovers to baseline
```
No node-level dumps yet, attaching logs in support ticket.

jamie_sre: @dan_engineer tagging — fractional MIG + bursty traffic smells like KV cache thrash + SM saturation when slices share L2/L3. Can we get nvidia-smi pmon and nvml top for the host around 09:12-09:24? Also check CGROUP throttles and IRQ steps.

infra-bot: autoscaler:event: {"pool":"pool-34-eu2","action":"scale_up","from":2,"to":3,"reason":"p95_threshold","trigger_ts":"2026-03-16T09:22:50Z","latency_slo":0.5}

sara_support: Minimal repro I ran in staging that looks similar: flood the endpoint with 512-token context at 120 rps for 90s and you see p95 drift after ~40s. Repro script: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 540); do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"'$(head -c 1024 /dev/urandom | base64)'"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.75
 done
```
When I pinned the same q4 variant on a single fractional host the KV cache misses spike in telemetry.

dan_engineer: Good repro, thanks. Two working hypotheses: (1) KV cache warmup pattern + fractional MIG leads to cache fragmentation across slices causing extra mem copies and kernel stalls; (2) packing/backlog causes long sequence batched kernels that block inference for other slices and produce 429s when queue fills.

dan_engineer: Can someone run this query and paste the output?
```
# prometheus-ish query pseudo:
max_over_time(gpu_sm_util[1m]) by (host)
max_over_time(gpu_mem_bw[1m]) by (host)
rate(kv_cache_miss_total[1m]) by (model_variant)
```
Would like the host-level max and the model variant miss rate between 09:10 and 09:25.

lucy_cs: Pasted outputs from console (trimmed): 
- host h-eu2-92: max_sm_util 98% at 09:14
- host h-eu2-92: mem_bw spike 15GB/s at 09:13-09:15
- model open-vicuna-30b-quant:q4: kv_cache_miss rate 240/min during window

jamie_sre: SM 98% + high mem bw + high kv misses = noisy neighbor causing eviction/serialization. Also check whether host had other tenants with kernels pinned to same SMs (see co-residency map).

ops_oncall: I just checked co-residency: h-eu2-92 had three fractional tenants at 09:12: brightbeam-102 (our tenant), sprite-ops (p99 < 200ms), and beta-loadgen (synthetic warmup generator). Beta-loadgen had a large batched job that started at 09:10. We should isolate suspicion to loadgen.

sara_support: If beta-loadgen was synthetic, it could have been kicked off by nightly jobs in the tenant workspace. Suggest we repro by running brightbeam load alone on that host and then with loadgen concurrently. If the spike disappears when isolated, we confirm noisy neighbor.

dan_engineer: Agreed. Next steps: 
1) Request customer tenant move to another reserved slot (soft migration) to confirm host-level fault. Can we schedule a quick live migration to an empty slice?
2) If migration mitigates, we propose policy change: avoid placing heavy batched synthetic tenants on same fractional-host slices as production q4 variants.
3) Add guardrail to autoscaler: prefer scaling within host-family before adding another fractional slice that increases co-residency.

lucy_cs: Customer approved a test migration window 09:45-10:00. I'll coordinate.

infra-bot: placement:move_request: {"from_host":"h-eu2-92","to_host":"h-eu2-101","tenant":"brightbeam-102","priority":"high","requested_by":"lucy_cs","ts":"2026-03-16T09:37:12Z"}

jamie_sre: Quick checklist for the move and validation: 
- Run nvidia-smi dmon during and after migration.
- Check kv_cache_miss for model variant pre/post.
- Trace any 429s and map to queue depth.
- If host still saturated after migration, collect kernel-level perf using Nsight counters.

sara_support: I pushed a short harness to staging for deterministic repro. I'll run the isolated vs cohost experiment during the migration window and report.

ops_oncall: FYI I scoped an immediate isolation: increased ospolicy to prevent batch-jobs > 4k tokens on hosts with production q4 tenants. We'll monitor for false positives.

lucy_cs: Customer reports migration completed and tail returned to baseline after ~90s. No 429s observed post-move. They said: "Thanks — performance normalized after moving off host h-eu2-92".

dan_engineer: Conclusion: noisy neighbor (beta-loadgen) on fractional MIG host caused KV cache/memory-bandwidth contention resulting in p95 spikes and transient 429s. Action items: 
- infra: add scheduling rule to avoid synthetic high-batch jobs on co-resident fractional hosts with q4 variants (infra ticket INF-4721).
- platform: add telemetry alert for kv_cache_miss rate > 100/min for production slots.
- support: reach out to customer with RCA and mitigation steps.

lucy_cs: I'll file RCA and send to BrightBeam. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

jamie_sre: Adding note — long-term we should consider smarter slice-aware KV cache allocation to avoid cross-slice thrash. Filed RFC draft."
